NOTICES OF PROPOSED RULEMAKING

The APA requires an agency file a Notice of Rulemaking Docket Opening which outlines its rulemaking intentions under A.R.S. § 41-1021. A docket opening and Notice of Proposed Rulemaking are often filed at the same time and published in the same Register issue. If they are not filed at the same time, information on where the docket opening was published is listed in the preamble of the proposed rulemaking.

An agency must allow at least 30 days to elapse after the publication of the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking in the Register before scheduling any oral proceedings. Written public comments shall be accepted for at least 30 days after the published notice. Refer to A.R.S. §§ 41-1013, 41-1022 and 41-1023.

Questions about the notice can be answered by the person listed in item #5 of the preamble.

Refer to item #11 for information on how to comment on this notice, the close of record to comment, and information related to oral proceedings.

ARTICLE 5. PROPOSED RULEMAKING

R1-1-503. Public Participation and Comment Period in Rulemaking

The public comment period for a proposed rule begins on the day the rule is published in the Register. An agency shall allow a minimum of 30 days for public comment after publication. After the end of the public comment period, an agency may hold an oral proceeding.

A. An agency shall determine if the law requires it to provide a person with the opportunity to comment on a notice.
B. If required to collect comments, an agency shall:
1. Notify the public about the opportunity to comment, either orally or in writing;
2. Provide information on how the agency will accept in writing statements, arguments, data and views on the proposed rule. For example, mailed, dropped off in person, emailed, or other electronic submission; and
3. When applicable, notify the public of the schedule of one or more oral proceedings.
C. An agency shall follow the timeframe requirements prescribed under the law when accepting public comments and scheduling oral proceedings.
1. Regular Proposed Rulemaking:
a. Requirement: A.R.S. § 41-1023(B) through (D).
b. Comment Period Begins: Publication of notice in the Register.
c. Length of Comment Period: For at least 30 days after publication of the notice.
d. Oral Proceeding. To notify the public, an agency shall prepare and file a Notice of Oral Proceeding on Proposed Rulemaking, available for download at www.azsos.gov/rules.
2. Expedited Rulemaking:
i. Requirement: A.R.S. § 41-1027.
ii. Comment Period Begins: Refer to A.R.S. § 41-1027(C).
iii. Length of Comment Period: An agency shall allow any person to provide written comment for at least thirty days after posting the notice.
iv. Oral Proceeding: Not applicable to this notice, but an agency shall respond to any written comment.
v. Objection Received: If an objection to an expedited rulemaking is received, an agency shall prepare and file a Notice of an Objection to an Expedited Rulemaking, using the Division template available for download at www.azsos.gov/rules.
c. Exempt Rulemaking:
i. Requirement: A.R.S. § 41-1005 or A.R.S. § 41-1097 or as provided under statute, session law, Arizona Constitution, or court order.
ii. Comment Period Begins: Most exempt rulemakings do not require a comment period. Refer to the specific exemption. An agency shall consult its agency head or counsel to determine the regulated requirements.
iii. Length of Comment Period: Refer to the specific exemption. An agency shall consult its agency head or counsel to determine the regulated requirements.
iv. Oral Proceeding: Refer to the specific exemption. An agency shall consult its agency head or counsel to determine the regulated requirements.

## Attend a Public Meeting
Attend an public meeting, known as an oral proceeding, being conducted by the agency on a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking.

A proceeding may be listed in the Preamble of a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking or an agency may inform the public of a meeting in a Notice of Oral Proceeding. Attend the meeting and be prepared to speak and comment.

An agency may not have a public meeting scheduled on the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking. If not, you may request the agency schedule a proceeding. This request must be put in writing within 30 days after the published Notice of Proposed Rulemaking.

Refer to information in the Preamble.

## Write the Agency
Put your comments in writing and send them to the agency. In order for the agency to consider your comments, the agency must receive them by the close of record. The comment must be received within the 30-day comment timeframe following the *Register* publication of the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking.
The agency opens the comment period to last at least 30 days. Written comments are accepted informally. The notice may contain information about oral proceedings. A proceeding is held no sooner than 30 days after the notice is published. If no proceeding is scheduled, the agency provides information on how a person may request to speak to the agency in person.

### Agency Stops the Process
The agency terminates its docket, or allows the docket to expire by not filing a proposed rule within one year.

### Agency Stops the Process
Agency decides not to proceed and does not file final rule with G.R.R.C. within one year after proposed rule is published. A.R.S. § 41-1021(A)(4)  
Agency decides not to proceed and files Notice of Termination of Rulemaking for publication in *Register*. A.R.S. § 41-1021(A)(2).

### Substantial Change
When an agency decides to make substantial changes to a proposed rule, it continues the process as provided under the APA. The agency obtains permission to proceed with a supplemental notice from the governor. The agency prepares a Notice of Supplemental Proposed Rulemaking and files it for publication in the *Register*.

### Close of Record
After evaluating public comments and conducting an internal review of the rule, an agency shall determine whether the rulemaking:
1. Requires a substantial change.  
2. Be submitted for review in a Notice of Final Rulemaking; or  
3. Should be terminated.

### Oral Proceeding
An person requests an agency to conduct an oral proceeding. The agency prepares a Notice of Oral Proceeding on Proposed Rulemaking, schedules one or more proceeding, and files the notice for publication in the *Register*. When it occurs, an agency usually extends the public comment period.

### Deadline to Submit Notice for Review
The Notice of Final Rulemaking must be submitted for review within 120 days after the close of record.

### Submission
A final rulemaking package is submitted by the agency to G.R.R.C. or A.G. for review and approval.

### Time Frame for Approval or Disapproval
G.R.R.C. has 90 days to review and approve or return the rule package, in whole or in part; A.G. has 60 days.

### Rule Approved ~ Published in *Register* and Codified in the Code
After approval by G.R.R.C. or A.G., the rule becomes effective 60 days after filing the notice with the Office of the Secretary of State, unless otherwise indicated in the Preamble of the notice. The Notice of Final Rulemaking is published in the *Register* and codified in the *Arizona Administrative Code*.
